messages:
amira: quick follow-up to the autoscaler RFC — what do folks think about the leader-election vs central-planner tradeoff for partitioned control-plane scenarios? specifically: how should dedicated pools behave if the control plane becomes unavailable for ~30s-5m?

chris: good call. central planner is simpler for consistent allocation, but single control-plane partitions are nasty. i'm leaning to: central planner for steady-state decisions + node-local fast-path that grants transient 'burst credits' when planner unreachable. fast-path should be eventually-consistent and conservative. :thinking:

sandeep: agree with hybrid. couple design constraints: 1) local fast-path must not violate tenant fairness long-term, 2) credits must be reclaimable once planner returns, 3) we need a clear audit trail for billing.

taylor: +1 hybrid. implementation sketch: node-agent keeps a small escrow pool (fractional_reserve) per tenant (eg 2-5% of pool GPU capacity). on planner disconnect, node-agent can hand out ephemeral leases from escrow with TTL and monotonic lease-id. when planner reconnects it reconciles by subtracting used-escrow from tenant's committed capacity.

amira: that sounds promising. couple Qs: how to prevent a noisy tenant from exhausting all escrows across nodes? also how to surface this to Dedicated contract/accounting?

chris: limit via per-tenant escrow budget + per-node cap. e.g., tenant escrow = min(configured_headroom, pool_size * 0.03). and admissions check: if tenant uses > X% of its escrow across nodes, refuse further ephemeral leases until planner is back.

sandeep: reconciling billing: record ephemeral-lease events locally (compact log) and stream a reconciliation batch to control plane when connectivity resumes. control plane applies idempotent adjustments. need to define reconciliation ops: {tenant, node, lease_id, duration_tokens, used_tokens}.

amira: can we make reconciliation idempotent? race if planner reboots and loses last applied offset. propose each lease_id encodes node_ts + counter and planner dedup by lease_id. also planner keeps per-node watermark to avoid replay.

chris: sounds good. another failure mode: split-brain where two planner leaders both think they control different subsets. we probably need leader-election with lease TTL, but still accept that short overlapping decisions may occur. ensure safety by making local fast-path conservative and by making planner reconciliation able to detect negative headroom and trigger corrective preemptions.

taylor: operational story: add a "degraded-mode" flag in the console and API for tenants so SRE/customer-support can see when ephemeral leases were used. default retention for logs should be 7d unless enterprise asks for longer.

amira: API surface: propose a read-only route for node health + escrow snapshots (for debugging only). not exposed to customers by default. also a metric: ephemeral_lease_grants{tenant,node,reason}.

chris: admission interface changes: central planner will continue to accept long-lived reservations and steady allocations. add a fast-path RPC: NodeAgent.RequestEphemeral(tenant, requested_tokens, ttl_ms) -> {granted_tokens, lease_id}. NodeAgent enforces per-node caps. on connectivity, planner can call NodeAgent.RefundEphemeral(lease_id) or consume usage. keep RPC idempotent.

sandeep: security: ephemeral leases must be signed by node-agent (HMAC) so planner can't be spoofed in reconciliation events. also encrypt reconciliation batches in transit.

amira: perf: we should microbench node-agent local decision latency — target <5ms for ephemeral grant decision to keep latency SLOs. also add metrics for reconciliation lag.

chris: rollout plan: feature-flag node-agent fast-path, start with internal tenants, then opt-in enterprise customers, then default on. need operator tooling to evict ephemeral leases gracefully (eg 30s warning + fallback to smaller model).

taylor: UX note: for Dedicated customers on reserved contracts, ephemeral usage should be shown separately and not charged as retries to committed quota. billing team needs the reconciliation format.

amira: ok agreed action items: 1) Chris + Sandeep draft proto for RequestEphemeral/RefundEphemeral and reconciliation payload, 2) Taylor draft console degraded-mode UI and metrics list, 3) I will add node-agent escrow prototype and microbench. we'll sync next week. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: node-agent/fastpath-canary deployed to staging (build 0.17.3)

chris: saw canary logs, initial latency looks good. spotted a minor bug where node_ts drift caused non-monotonic lease ids — will push fix.

sandeep: note for RFC doc: include explicit invariants and a 'recovery plan' section so ops can run playbook when reconciliation shows oversubscription.

amira: thanks everyone — will capture this thread into the follow-up RFC section and link to the proto PR when ready.
